extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO staff (OPAP/examiners)
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative and formal requirements for obtaining a filing date, handling informalities and drawings, procedures for unlocatable files, and rules governing payment, refunds, and deposit accounts at the USPTO. Covers OPAP drawing review, 37 CFR 1.251 unlocatable-file procedure, fee payment/itemization, and related administrative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of the provisional or nonprovisional application is the date of receipt in the Office of the application which includes a specification containing description pursuant to 37 CFR 1.71 and at least one claim (for nonprovisional applications) and any drawings required by 37 CFR 1.81(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any required items are missing, applicant will be notified to file them and the filing date will be the date of receipt of the missing part(s). If documents purporting to be a specification are so informal and incoherent that they would clearly not constitute a specification as required by 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or 37 CFR 1.71, the application will not be accorded a filing date until corrections are made; the filing date will then be the date corrections were made. Petitions to review a refusal to grant a filing date are by way of petition with applicable fee (37 CFR 1.17(f)); petitioner should provide arguments/evidence that items were not missing or that a filing date should be assigned regardless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal application definition and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is informal if typed on both sides of the paper, or is not permanent, legible, or reproducible. If such informalities are timely corrected, the application is given the filing date on which the original informal papers were filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP accords a filing date (as of the Office Date stamp) to application papers including a specification containing a description and at least one claim (for certain nonprovisional categories prior to March 18, 2013 and design applications) and a drawing, even if informal because they do not comply with rules/notices. OPAP will send a Notice (e.g., Notice to File Corrected Application Papers) requiring correction; failure to correct within the specified time results in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application cover sheet and amendment limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application which does not include a cover sheet (37 CFR 1.51(c)(1), which may be an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) or a cover letter, identifying the application as a provisional application) will be treated as a nonprovisional application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional application will not be examined. NOTE: No amendment, other than to make the provisional application comply with the patent statute and all applicable regulations, may be made to the provisional application after the filing date (see 37 CFR 1.53(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP drawing review standard
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP performs an initial review of drawings in new utility and plant patent applications to determine whether the drawings can be effectively scanned for publication purposes; design applications are not published and their drawings are not reviewed by OPAP for publication purposes. The standard is such that most drawings, including those indicated as "informal drawings," will be acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP inspects drawings to see if they can be effectively scanned and adequately reproduced. If unacceptable, OPAP will object and require corrected drawings within a set time period (usually two months). Corrected drawings must be filed in paper to the mailing address in the Notice along with any other items required to avoid abandonment; no fee is necessary for filing corrected drawings required by OPAP. Otherwise, patent publications and patents will reflect the quality of the drawings on filing unless applicant voluntarily submits better quality drawings (see MPEP § 1121).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific drawing defects that trigger OPAP objections (A–G)
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP may object to drawings if they: (A) have a line quality that is too light to be reproduced or illegible text (reference characters, sheet numbers, view numbers); (B) have missing lead lines (lines between reference characters and details); (C) contain excessive text or text that is not in English; (D) do not have appropriate margins or correct size paper (top/left/right/bottom margins and acceptable sheet sizes specified); (E) have more than one figure and each figure is not labeled 'Fig.' with a consecutive Arabic numeral or an Arabic numeral and capital letter; (F) include photographs capable of illustration by other mediums and illegible after scanning; (G) contain color drawings or color photographs without a petition to accept color drawings/photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to specific rules: 37 CFR 1.84(l),(p)(1) (line quality/legibility), 1.84(q) (lead lines), 1.84(o)/(p)(2) and 1.52(d) (text/language), 1.84(f)/(g) (margins/size), 1.84(u)(1) (figure labeling), 1.84(b) (photographs). Note elimination of requirement for black-and-white photocopy of color drawings/photographs; color requires petition if not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing correction filing requirements and abandonment risk
rubrics_metrics.description: If OPAP objects and sends a Notice requiring submission of corrected drawings within a set time period (usually two months), corrected drawings must be filed in paper to the mailing address in the Notice along with any other items required by OPAP to avoid abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee is necessary for filing corrected drawings required by OPAP. If corrections are not timely made, the application may be abandoned. Publications/patents will usually reflect the drawings as filed unless better quality drawings are voluntarily submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic scanning and Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications are electronically scanned and loaded into the Image File Wrapper (IFW) system upon filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once documents are loaded into IFW, examiners, technical support staff, and other Office personnel perform further processing and examination using IFW. For handling of models, exhibits, and specimens see relevant MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlocatable file procedure (37 CFR 1.251) — applicant responses
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office cannot locate the file of an application, patent, or other patent-related proceeding after a reasonable search, the Office will notify the applicant or patentee and set a time period within which applicant must comply by: (1) providing a copy of applicant’s/patentee’s record of all correspondence between the Office and applicant (except U.S. patent documents), a list of such correspondence, and a statement that the copy is complete and accurate; (2) producing the record for the Office to copy and providing a statement that the papers produced are the complete record; or (3) stating that applicant/patentee does not possess any record of correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.251 applies to any type of application and status. If an applicant chooses to produce records for copying, bring them to the Customer Service Center in OPAP. Appendix or information disclosure statements submitted with an application are not in the Office’s database and must be provided by applicant/patentee (except in limited circumstances). The Office may also attempt informal contact to obtain missing documents before issuing a 1.251 notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlocatable file procedure — time periods and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will set a time period of three months for reply in a notice under 37 CFR 1.251 in an application; this period is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a) by three months up to a maximum of six months in an application. For a patent, the time period for reply is six months and is not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply within the set time in an application will result in abandonment of the application. If an applicant fails to reply within three months, any patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) will be reduced by the number of days beginning the day after the three-month point until filing the reply. If a patent owner fails to comply, the Office may only be able to produce a certified copy of the patent and application-as-filed, possibly affecting enforcement. The Office may pursue actions under 37 CFR 41.128 or 37 CFR 11.18 if the patent is involved in an Office proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees payable in advance and itemization requirement (37 CFR 1.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent fees and charges payable to the USPTO are required to be paid in advance at the time of requesting any action for which a fee is payable, except that under 37 CFR 1.53 applications for patent may be assigned a filing date without payment of the basic filing fee. All fees paid must be itemized in each individual application, patent, or proceeding so it is clear for which purpose the fees are paid; the Office may return fees that are not itemized as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The itemization requirement is intended to clarify how fees should be applied; generic references like 'filing fee(s)' can be sufficient when clear. In some situations (e.g., a paper filed after filing date), referring to ‘filing fee(s)’ can cover surcharges under 37 CFR 1.16. In petitions for extensions of time filed without a specifically itemized fee but with general authorization to charge a deposit account, it is clear what fee is needed and the deposit account may be charged appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and form of payment (37 CFR 1.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments shall be made in U.S. dollars and in acceptable forms: cashier’s or certified check, Treasury note, national bank notes, or United States Postal Service money order. Payments may also be made by credit card (except for replenishing a deposit account). Checks and money orders must be payable to the Director of the USPTO. Payments from foreign countries must be payable and immediately negotiable in the U.S.; money sent by mail is at the sender’s risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sent in any other form the Office may delay or cancel credit until collection. The Office will accept checks payable to the Commissioner of Patents and Trademarks for now. The Office may return fees that are not itemized as required by 37 CFR 1.22(b). See also specific credit-card guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds of fees (37 CFR 1.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may refund any fee paid by mistake or in excess of that required. A change of purpose after payment (e.g., withdrawing a filing) will not entitle a party to a refund. The Office will not refund amounts of $25 or less unless specifically requested. Any request for refund must be filed within two years from the date the fee was paid (except as otherwise provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refunds of fees paid by credit card will be by credit to the card charged. If banking information for electronic funds transfer is not provided, the Director may require such information or use payment instrument banking info. Specific reexamination refund rules: (1) ex parte reexamination filing fee refunded less the fee in 1.20(c)(7) if Director decides not to institute; (2) inter partes refund of $7,970 if not instituted; (3) supplement exam: reexamination-ordered fee returned if Director decides not to institute reexamination. Request should indicate form of refund (check, EFT, credit to deposit account).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of application of insufficient payment — nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When a payment submitted for fees due on filing in a nonprovisional application is insufficient and applicant has not specified application of the payment, the Office will apply the payment in the following order until expended: (1) basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(a),(b),(c),(e)); (2) non-electronic filing fee (1.16(t)); (3) non-DOCX fee (1.16(u)); (4) application size fee (1.16(s)); (5) late filing surcharge (1.16(f)); (6) processing fee for application filed in language other than English (1.17(i)); (7) search fee (1.16(k),(l),(m),(n)); (8) examination fee (1.16(o),(p),(q),(r)); (9) excess claims fee (1.16(h),(i),(j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intent is to apply payments in a consistent order when the payor has not specified fee application. See MPEP § 607 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of application of insufficient payment — provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When payment submitted for fees due on filing in a provisional application is insufficient and applicant has not specified application, the Office will apply the payment in the following order until expended: (1) basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(d)); (2) application size fee (1.16(s)); (3) late filing surcharge (1.16(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also MPEP § 607 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: National stage (35 U.S.C. 371) basic national fee priority (37 CFR 1.492/1.495)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.492 specifies required fees for international applications entering the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371. The basic national fee must be paid prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date to the United States; this time period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant makes a payment in a national stage application prior to 30 months but does not specify a sufficient amount for the basic national fee, the Office will apply the payment first to the basic national fee regardless of applicant’s specification (i.e., payment applied to the basic national fee as priority). This is distinguished from U.S. national filings under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) where a basic filing fee may be accepted later with a surcharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit card payment form, security, transaction limits, and record handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Credit Card Payment Form (PTO-2038) should be used when paying a patent process or trademark process fee by credit card, unless payment is made using the USPTO patent electronic filing system. Credit card payments via the USPTO website must include the 3- or 4-digit security code. The Department of the Treasury imposes a transaction maximum for individual credit card payments and multiple payments made to U.S. Government entities on the same day; effective June 1, 2015, the maximum is $24,999.99.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Credit Card Payment Form will not be included among records open to public inspection. If credit card information is provided on other forms/documents, that information may become part of the public file. The Office will not accept oral (telephonic) instructions to complete the Credit Card Payment Form or otherwise charge a patent/trademark process fee to a credit card. Any refund of a fee paid by credit card will be by credit to the account charged. If the security code cannot be read, contact the issuing financial institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit accounts (37 CFR 1.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit accounts may be established for convenience in paying fees and ordering services. A minimum deposit of $1,000 is required for general deposit accounts; a minimum deposit of $300 may be paid to establish a restricted subscription deposit account used exclusively for subscription order of patent copies as issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At month-end a deposit account statement is rendered; remittance must be made promptly upon receipt to cover charges and restore the account to its normal deposit value. An amount sufficient to cover all requested fees/services/copies must always be on deposit. Charges to accounts with insufficient funds will not be accepted. A service charge will be assessed for each month the balance at month-end is below the applicable minimum ($1,000 general; $300 restricted subscription). Filing/issue/appeal/international charges and other specifics governed by 37 CFR 1.25 and related provisions.
